summary: This bill mandates that private health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, and Federal Employees Health Benefits plans cover HIV prevention services, including PrEP and PEP medications, related administrative fees, lab tests, counseling, and clinical follow-up, without any cost-sharing or preauthorization requirements (unless a therapeutically equivalent drug is covered without preauthorization).

scores.thoughts: This bill mandates no-cost coverage for HIV prevention services (PrEP and PEP) across private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, and Federal Employees Health Benefits programs. This expands access to specific healthcare services, moving towards a more publicly supported healthcare model for HIV prevention.

The bill expands coverage for HIV prevention services under Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, which are key components of the social safety net. By eliminating cost-sharing and deductibles for these services, it effectively expands welfare benefits related to healthcare access for vulnerable populations.

The bill focuses on increasing access to specific prescription drugs (PrEP and PEP) for HIV prevention by mandating no-cost coverage. This is a healthcare access issue rather than a drug enforcement or regulation policy, so it does not directly impact drug policy in terms of enforcement or legality of substances.

The bill mandates new no-cost coverage requirements under Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, increasing federal outlays without any offsetting revenue or spending reductions, thereby accepting larger deficits to expand access.

The entire bill requires government programs and private plans to cover PrEP, PEP, and related HIV prevention services with zero cost-sharing or deductibles, directly using federal mandates to lower patient costs and expand coverage.
